contact_edits.before: Neither the play nor its author are dismissible; Orton, unlike the self-satisfied rebels of London's Royal Court, was a real subversive, a working-class gay man who'd done time and ended up being bludgeoned to death by his lover. He had a genuine outsider's vision, one most completely and resourcefully expressed in his next and last play What the Butler Saw. Loot works perfectly on its own terms, but they're narrow terms. One personal complaint. When Truscott discovers Mrs. McLeavy's preserved corpse he asks, "whose mummy is this?" to which Hal replies, truthfully but without thinking, "mine." I always thought that was the funniest line in the play. It isn't here; the timing is off. But that doesn't happen often. - Loot is in repertory at the Young Centre through Aug. 1. Call 416-866-8666 for tickets and information.
